parsed.explanation: Strong operative protections - X markers, bathroom guidance, hate-crime law, self-declared custody preference, courts awarding damages and extending femicide law - with no criminalisation or documented entry screening. Significant violence and discrimination in practice, one-state evidence of masculine-unit custody despite the national resolution, and a reinstated minors care ban keep it below the 0.85 tier: recourse works but street and custody exposure remains real.

entry_documents.protection: X/unspecified marker required on government ID since Jan 2024; spousal-visa and immigration recognition equal nationwide; no trans-specific entry screening documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; domestic marker rules mainly signal institutional acceptance, no documented border mismatch practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One-state 2021 census of 138 travesti/trans-women inmates found housing in masculine units, some neutral/security units, characterised as double punishment with recurring rights violations.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2020/2021 national judicial resolution: self-declaration, reasoned placement after consulting preference among male, female or LGBTI-specific units, recorded preference, transfers prioritised on threat, no isolation in LGBTI spaces.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Documented practice diverges from national norm in that state system; visitor detention placement is uncertain outside it.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Some states/municipalities passed school gender/sexuality course bans, though courts have overturned them since 2020.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Official guidance affirms bathrooms matching identity; courts fine businesses discriminating, e.g. nightclub refusing trans woman entry held liable for moral damages.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National guidance and court enforcement mitigate local facility friction, but local bans show variation.

care_services.exposure: Adult public surgery requires age 21+, no personality-disorder diagnosis and 2 years psychological evaluation; waiting lines and poorly equipped facilities push to private care.
care_services.protection: Public surgery free as constitutional right; July 2026 ruling requires insurance cover for facial feminisation surgery.
care_services.interaction: Access is legally protected but practically constrained; urgency/continuity may be delayed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: March 2026 review records significant violence and discrimination in practice; legislative opposition, Catholic/evangelical intolerance sources and death threats against a gay representative documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2018 no-surgery LGR ruling; 2019 supreme court: transphobia punishable as racism, discrimination/hate crimes on gender identity prohibited; nationwide anti-discrimination framework.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law is protective on paper and partly enforced by courts, but social/political hostility persists.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 medical council banned gender-affirming care for minors; Oct 2025 judge overturned the block and reinstated ban; medication continuity and interstate travel for care remain live issues.
minors_guardians.protection: A state court briefly restored care nationwide July 2025; constitutional challenge pending; schools must combat homotransphobic bullying (June 2024).
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor faces documented care-continuity uncertainty, not criminal exposure for the adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Majority of physical violence against LGBTQIA+ people in largest city at night; drink-spiking robberies documented May 2024 ahead of Pride; dating-app robbery schemes have been fatal; threats/intimidation around Oct 2024 municipal elections.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Courts upheld moral-damage award against discriminating nightclub; high court unanimously extended domestic-violence and femicide laws to trans women; municipal inquiry issued 189 recommendations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is documented but courts have shown willingness to remedy discrimination and extend protective law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Minors litigation unresolved; prison census covers one state only and does not establish other states; no trans-disaggregated homicide rate with denominator sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts, awards and extensions show recourse operating in commercial and protective-law cases.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns prevent a higher score but do not negate documented protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: equality protections and police/court recourse coexist with documented night-time physical attacks and remedies dependent on reporting; this case has stronger custody-preference and bathroom guidance, similar street risk.

Lower than 0.85-A: that anchor shows prompt discipline, broad tolerance and only isolated friction, whereas this dossier records significant violence/discrimination in a 2026 review and one-state masculine custody practice.

Higher than 0.65-B: that anchor centres on repeated refusal with slow remedy; here no documented systematic care refusal for adults, bathroom and X-marker protections are explicit, and courts award damages promptly in documented cases.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is protective at entry, facilities and in court, with self-declared custody preference as a strong formal mitigation. Its operative limits are street violence and discrimination despite law, documented divergence from custody norms in one state prison system, and the reinstated minors care ban affecting travelling families. Rule of law works for documented claimants, so hostility is discounted but not erased, placing the case in Reduced Risk near its lower end.
